basis: Progressive skeletal-muscle dystrophy; swallowing dysfunction affects 12/32 (~38%). Respiratory insufficiency occurs in only 3/32 (~9%); conduction defects are not typical.
Focal pancreatic beta-cell hyperinsulinism causes hypoglycemia; common permanent neurologic injury is not established for this subtype.
Ependymal tumor originates in the brain or spinal cord; extracranial organ tumors are very rare.
Hereditary amyloidosis defines neuropathy and infiltrative cardiomyopathy; nephropathy occurs in 30-79%. Ocular and gastrointestinal dysfunction also qualify but are omitted by cap.
AQP4-antibody-mediated CNS disease; myelitis and optic neuritis are defining manifestations.
Carotid arterial narrowing defines the disease; cerebral infarction is a separately diagnosed complication, not universal organ involvement.
Carcinoma originates in the esophagus.
Malignant mesenchymal tumor arises within the central nervous system; mesenchymal histology does not establish locomotor-system involvement.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay define the disorder. Joint hypermobility in 3/10 does not establish musculoskeletal damage.
Inherited peripheral axonal/demyelinating neuropathy; persistent distal muscle wasting and foot deformities affect most patients (>30%).
Disease is localized to the corneal stroma, with linear infiltrates and possible scarring; no established immune etiology.
Branchiootic syndrome is defined by ear malformations and hearing impairment; renal disease is not characteristic of this syndrome.
Ichthyosis and deficient gonadal hormone function are the defining manifestations.
Silver deposition is localized to the cornea; ocular is the primary disease site even when deposits do not impair vision.
Cardiac, skeletal and CNS malformations characterize the syndrome; renal hypoplasia/aplasia is annotated 80-99%. Ocular, otologic and oral abnormalities omitted by cap.
Inherited transmissible prion disease causes cerebral amyloid deposition, progressive ataxia and dementia; weakness reflects neurologic disease.
Severe intellectual disability and primordial skeletal growth restriction define the syndrome; strabismus occurs in 4/9 (~44%). Skin and facial dysmorphism lack established functional damage.
Congenital absence or severe hypoplasia of mitral valve leaflets causes mitral regurgitation.
Alpha-sarcoglycan muscular dystrophy damages skeletal muscle. Definition explicitly states cardiac and respiratory involvement are rare; isolated 1/1 reports do not establish prevalence.
Limb and vertebral malformations plus structural dental defects define the syndrome. Auricular and skin dysmorphism do not establish additional functional damage.
Fibroblastic soft-tissue sarcoma arises in connective tissues, typically deep locomotor soft tissues; no other organ involvement is established across the group.
Defined by enlargement of renal parenchyma.
Reduced cerebrospinal fluid pressure is a CNS disorder; occasional hearing loss and cranial nerve palsies do not establish common additional organ damage.
Early osteoporosis and neurodevelopmental impairment define the disorder: osteopenia 5/5, developmental delay 6/6, with common microcephaly and spasticity.
Sphingolipid storage; hepatic infiltration 80-99%, cytopenias 2/2 with splenic disease 3/3, seizures 30-79%. Skeletal disease, including osteopenia in 1/2, omitted by cap.
